title: Amjad Masad on Going Direct, Building Replit, and the Future of Software

reader_summary.headline: Amjad Masad shares lessons on building Replit and navigating online criticism.
reader_summary.overview: Amjad Masad explains how founders should tell stories larger than their company to survive early struggles. He advises practicing public speaking early and staying visible during controversies. Masad also discusses the importance of understanding current debates before posting content online.

key_points.text: Practicing public speaking and making mistakes early helps founders get used to attention before they grow.
key_points.evidence_quote: The best way to get desensitized is to just make a fool of yourself every day doing improv.

key_points.text: Understanding the current debate is harder and more important than actually posting content.
key_points.evidence_quote: The thing that's time consuming is understanding what is the larger debate because the way to go viral is to couch or dress up your argument, your world vie

key_points.text: Own your mistakes quickly to turn a bad story into a positive one.
key_points.evidence_quote: I think the right thing to do was to own up to it. The fact that we didn't have development production separation is a bad thing. And two days later, we rolled out that fixed.
